Inventory with AU codes

CSV that already has an analysis-unit column (e.g. AU_NS, AU_PRS, yFU_NatSucn_AU) and preferably hectares. Two-part codes such as BW1_PO1 and four-part codes such as SB1_Seed_SB1_LC1 both work.

How the codes are written

Planning teams encode pathways differently. Pick the column and the pattern. The default unit list is NER Boreal; replace it if your FMU uses other codes.

Leave empty to count records. Shape_Area is treated as m² → ha.

Proportions are within each current unit (rows of BW1 sum to 100%).

Inventory and lookup

Two CSVs. The lookup holds stratum keys (e.g. PLANFU + DEVSTAGE), the value to write (e.g. AU_PRS), and a proportion that sums to 100 within each stratum. The inventory gets that column filled so area shares match — polygons are not split.

Excel must be saved as CSV UTF-8 first.

Column mapping

Stratum columns join the two files. Default area is HA / AREA_HA / Shape_Area. Output name is whatever you want written onto the inventory.

45 / 55 or 0.45 / 0.55. Groups that do not sum to 100% are normalized.
Shape_Area is treated as m² → ha. None = count polygons (not recommended).
Same seed + same files = same assignment.
Limit forest units in inventory ·

Optional for small files. Required for inventories of about 200 MB or more — the browser cannot hold a 900 MB table.

Assignment is by area within each stratum, then shuffled. Whole polygons stay whole.

Inventory strata not in the lookup

Present in the inventory (after POLYTYPE filter) but no lookup row. Those polygons were left unassigned.

Lookup strata not in the inventory

Present in the lookup but no matching inventory rows were assigned. Check spelling, DEVSTAGE coding, and the POLYTYPE filter.
